unknowns: Whether the original engine wrote any persistent derived artefact during a normal mission load, and what it keyed it on, is unmeasured. The static audit found no such writer, path, import or vocabulary, but a negative over static spans cannot exclude a run-time-assembled path, a DLL writing on the engine's behalf, a script-invoked GameZ write that is later read back, or an unenumerated code path. What would settle it is an owner-run file-system trace of the original executable during one mission load (Process Monitor file events, with the executable digest and the written-path list). See docs/findings/2026-10-27-f15-f-original-cache-and-keys.md, 'The unknown, and what would settle it'.

review.identity: deepseek-1 (implementer); no reviewer has run yet
review.method: Every field is derived from the recorded run: candidate_tree from HEAD^{tree} on a clean checkout, the counts and assertion statuses from tests.log (the same selection the finding documents), the probe artifacts from the read-only probe over $CS_ENGINE_IMAGE, and install_sha256/content_sha256 from a production cs-inspect inventory of the same $CS_GAME_DIR in the same session. Nothing is typed in. SCOPE: this is static analysis of the original image plus retail data; no original executable ran, so the claim is 'implemented', never 'verified_original', and the artifact-level result is an explicit unknown about original run-time behaviour, not a negative claim about it. tools/validate_evidence.py is run without --require-pass on purpose: the deliverable is itself an explicit unknown, so the structural check (every artifact hash, every count) is the applicable one, and dropping the unknown from machine-readable evidence to make --require-pass green is exactly what the owner directive forbids.
